chapter_theme: The jnani's action (ஞானி செயல்): the knowers of tattva who know themselves exhaust past karma by living it out and stop future karma from forming, by Siva's grace placed on their head; karma arises through mind, speech and body and does not last when mind and speech stand straight.

2610.reading: When former karma arrives, the knowers of tattva who know themselves experience it first and are rid of it; later karma they watch closely so as to drive it off, because they direct the five senses toward the good.
2610.nuance: முன்னை வினை and பின்னை வினை are taken as karma already made, which must be lived out (உண்டே நீங்குவர், 'having eaten it they are free'), and karma not yet made, which can be prevented. The verse does not say the jnani escapes former karma, only that he exhausts it.

2611.reading: The knowers of tattva who know themselves untie the knot of former karma and seize and crush later karma, by the grace of Siva placed on their head.
2611.nuance: The verse repeats 2610's first line and adds the cause: சென்னியில் வைத்த சிவனருள், grace placed on the head, recalling the guru placing the Lord's feet on the disciple's head. முடிச்சை அவிழ் (untie the knot) may mean that former karma loses its binding power rather than that it is not experienced.

2612.reading: Strong karma kindles through mind, speech and body; if mind and speech stand straight, strong karma does not last; the jnani is the one fit to change himself and act, free of the latent tendencies of those whose mind and speech have gone astray.
2612.nuance: The first two lines are clear and set mind, speech and body as the three doors of karma. The last two are compressed: மனவாக்கு கெட்டவர் may be those whose mind and speech are corrupt or those in whom mind and speech have ceased, and வாதனை (vasana, latent impressions) may be what the jnani escapes or what he works through.

links.note: 2610 says how the jnani deals with former and later karma; 2611 says by what power: Siva's grace placed on the head.
Both have the wise meet arriving karma calmly: the Naladiyar's wise take it as old debt and are freed of confusion, Tirumular's jnanis live it out and are rid of it.

The Kural says nothing is stronger than what is apportioned, which arrives before any scheme to avoid it. Tirumular grants that former karma must be lived out, but adds that the jnani can stop karma not yet made, which the Kural's verse does not address.
Both free the Lord's own from the hold of deeds: in the Kural the two kinds of deed do not cling to those who praise him, in Tirumular the jnani unties former karma by Siva's grace.

source_issues: 2610: line 3 reads தததுவ, a misprint for தத்துவ (as in 2611).
